asham.nature: Obligatory private offering, edible priestly remainder, six types and bounded doubtful-offence scope follow Intro18/35/36/41 and Mishnah5:5.
asham.types: Inspected all six labeled items, including oath prerequisite for theft, inadvertent misuse, nazir impurity versus completion, poor metzora, and doubtful-offence exception.
asham.animals: Yearlings for nazir/metzora and explicit two-year asham talui follow the identified MT4:22 witness. No unnamed alternative edition is asserted.
asham.service: North requirement and boundaries follow Z5:1; split hand/vessel reception is preserved without calling altar application hazaah.
asham.eating: Burned emurim and male-priest courtyard consumption until midnight follow the attached introduction and Mishnah.
asham.talui-depth: Examples reproduce the Mishnah's listed doubts; final qualification prevents treating every doubtful prohibition as an asham obligation.

public-shelamim.purpose: Exclusive identification as two Shavuot lambs follows Intro25 and Z5:5.
public-shelamim.service: North and two applications/four sides are retained; comparison to chattat expressly excludes its four applications.
public-shelamim.portions: Priestly courtyard/time limits are distinguished from private shelamim owner consumption in Jerusalem.

minchah.nature: Kometz, vessel and remainder are restricted to a minchah requiring kemitzah; analogy to slaughter/emurim is bounded.
minchah.eating: All-courtyard kemitzah and male-priest eating limits follow Mishnah6:1; uneaten menachot are separated.
minchah.cohen: Rabbi Shimon's kemitzah position and sages' uneaten-remainder criterion remain distinct; Rambam's ruling is stated.
minchah.matzah: Matzah requirement is limited to altar offerings; chametz todah bread and two loaves are correctly excluded from altar burning.
minchah.exceptions: Read both current paragraphs and all four witnesses. Omer contradiction remains explicit; full TYT comparison and Ikkar's explicit retraction wording are accurately separated.

av-holachah.act: Both paragraphs distinguish shelo-lishmah effects by offering type and bind piggul to its additional conditions.
av-holachah.possible: The possibility of omitting transport explains Rabbi Shimon's view; sages still classify performed transport as service.
av-holachah.thought: Rabbi Eliezer's required-versus-unneeded route distinction is reported as his view, which Rambam rejects; no route is reconstructed from difficult text.

t-met.source: Source lists different corpse components and cemetery; prose does not give every component the same threshold.
t-met.chain: Corpse-mediated av chains are preserved; earthenware exception is explicit.
t-met.scope: Gentile corpse contact versus tent rule is expressly attributed to Rambam; sanctuary/nazir consequences are not inferred from the av inventory.
t-met.kli-cheres: Both paragraphs distinguish metal examples from earthenware's rishon status and require material/mode/rank to be checked separately.

t-sheretz.species: Death qualification is supplied by separately attached Leviticus11:31; frogs/snakes remain outside the named eight.
t-sheretz.contact: Lentil threshold, no carrying transmission, stripped bones and four skin-as-flesh cases follow attached text.
t-sheretz.example: Bread rishon deoraita and food-to-food sheni derabbanan reproduce Rambam's explicit example; difficult general sentence is not used.

t-nevelah.source: Clean-slaughter distinction and exclusion of blood/stripped bones follow Intro5; marrow remains flesh.
t-nevelah.ways: Contact versus carrying and cessation of clothing transmission after separation follow the explicit source clauses; source's difficult contrary sentence stays noted.
t-nevelah.bird: Read Intro21 in full: swallowing threshold, no nevelah-contact transmission, separate food-impurity conditions and Rambam's eventual Torah-level conclusion remain distinct.

t-zav.source: Two versus three male sightings and female three-day rule are distinguished; named bodily fluids and bedding are actually listed.
t-zav.midras: Bedding/seating share midras while riding is distinct; stacked supports need no direct contact. No ruling is inferred from contradictory boel-zavah text.
t-zav.rank: A zav makes midras; an existing midras does not create another midras. Ordinary av transmission is separated from this special creation.

t-niddah.meaning: Seven niddah days and three-day out-of-period zavah requiring seven clean days follow verses and Niddah4:7.
t-niddah.distinction: Small zavah's one/two days, intercourse restriction, bedding impurity, and absence of large-zavah counting/sacrifice remain linked.
t-niddah.day-watch: Repeated distinction between one/two days and three consecutive days is faithful; no practical calendar is supplied.

t-contact.maga: Visible-body direct contact is distinguished from swallowing; source itself supplies that contrast.
t-contact.masa: Human carrying is distinguished from the vessel touching nevelah and from other vessels' mere participation in the load.
t-contact.heset: Nevelah tilting is treated as carrying, with sheretz exclusion and explicit warning that zav heset needs separate treatment.
t-contact.tilt: Beam example preserves actual lifting of the load; it does not generalize impurity to all nearby vessels.

t-ohel.meaning: Both paragraphs preserve half-measure nonjoining and the less-than-tefach compressed-impurity exception, including Rambam's ruling.
t-ohel.distinction: Read cited segments plus preceding definition of bib. Square tefach dimensions, naturally formed tents and outlet distinction remain source-bounded.
t-ohel.bib-example: Both bib outcomes are retained. A possible geometry concern was resolved by the source's explicit opening-in-house wording, so it is not an error finding.

t-ranks.rank: Av versus derivative rule follows the clear quoted maxim; difficult opposite introductory sentence remains disclosed in source note.
t-ranks.food: Terminal levels differ for hullin/terumah/kodesh; wording limits nontransmission to that chain rather than every possible liquid rule.
t-ranks.rabbinic: Torah origin of av is not confused with third/fourth levels; historical basar-taavah decree and its later form are both retained.
t-ranks.levels: Names of levels do not replace the hullin/terumah/kodesh distinction. No universal food-to-food Torah chain is introduced.

t-kelim.materials: Eight categories are listed, glass is rabbinic, and the completed-work rule is explicitly limited to the attached metal-vessel prooftext.
t-kelim.cheres: Airspace example and absence of av status follow Kelim1:1 and Intro14/31.
t-kelim.purification: Both paragraphs disclose the introductory generalization versus MT1:3 glass exception; no reconciliation or ruling about purchased-vessel immersion is invented.
t-kelim.glass: Glass's rabbinic origin is retained without transferring all metal/earthenware details to it.

t-hechsher.meaning: Pure preparatory wetting is distinguished from imparting impurity; no exclusive limitation to primary-source impure liquids remains.
t-hechsher.conditions: Detachment, consent, wet-at-later-consent, and impure-liquid simultaneous transmission are preserved. Rashi is separately attached and not quoted as Rambam.
t-hechsher.liquids: Seven liquids and excluded fruit juices follow Intro24; tevul-yom exception is expressly retained.

t-mashkin.seven: The named seven, rather than every physical liquid, govern this Rambam presentation.
t-mashkin.first: Serial liquid transmission keeps rishon status exactly as Intro24 describes; food ranks are not imported.
t-mashkin.tvul: Tevul-yom liquid exception and terumah versus hullin distinction remain explicit.

t-yadayim.meaning: Rabbinic hand decree, sheni status, and holy-writings example are bounded rather than making the whole body tamei.
t-yadayim.distinction: Rabbi Yehoshua's generalization is distinguished from sages' rejection; doubtful-hand cases have their separate attached source.

t-tevilah.water: Forty seah pooled-water requirement, flowing/sitting distinction and living-water requirements follow both Mikvaot passages.
t-tevilah.chatzitzah: Body and attached hair must be reached, with qualification that obstruction law has its conditions; no every-speck rule is claimed.
t-tevilah.sunset: Tevul-yom effects and certain rabbinic impurities needing no sunset are both stated.
t-tevilah.tvul-explanation: Terumah-pot versus hullin-pot example accurately separates immersion from sunset completion.

t-hazaah.water: Spring-water qualification follows Mikvaot1:8, not merely the broad term mayim; possible handling impurity is not universalized.
t-hazaah.days: Third/seventh-day requirement is directly in Numbers19:12; counting details remain deferred.
t-hazaah.mazzeh: Actual sprinkling condition is retained for the carrier; carrying threshold and unnecessary touching remain separate.

t-safek.meaning: Incomplete mikveh condition has separate MT4:6 prooftext; uncertainty whether three log fell differs from uncertainty about amount.
t-safek.distinction: Decree-based bodily impurity differs from contact with a rabbinic av; uncertain av such as beit-hapras has the no-burning exception.

i-kiddushin.meaning: Woman's consent is scoped to kiddushin in her authority; father's separate authority has its own prooftext and later explanation.
i-kiddushin.ways: Inspected species of kiddushin, coin threshold, document wording/witnesses, and penalized-but-effective intercourse kiddushin.
i-kiddushin.issur: Valid prohibited unions are distinguished from arayot without kiddushin; statement uses bounded examples rather than all prohibited unions.
i-kiddushin.way-of-act: Both paragraphs follow document medium/witness and vekyatzah-vehayetah analogy; no paper-only requirement is introduced.

i-yuchasin.map: Four Mishnah categories are distinguished by kiddushin validity and prohibited status without conflating those questions.
i-yuchasin.chalal: Chalal offspring in priestly prohibitions is distinguished from mamzer offspring, despite shared hapagum wording.
i-yuchasin.limits: Both paragraphs preserve slave/gentile mother result, ger-mamzer exception and bounded Egyptian/Edomite reference.

i-nissuin.stages: Meiri overview is supplemented by Ketubot4:4 for nourishment and usufruct after marriage.
i-nissuin.time: Clock starts with demand, with virgin/widow and maturity distinctions; no single universal waiting period is stated.
i-nissuin.example: Betrothed Israelite woman's terumah exclusion until huppah is explicit in Ketubot5:2.

i-ketubah.scope: Meiri distinguishes principal/addition and automatic versus stipulated terms; not all terms are treated as contractual additions.
i-ketubah.shiabud: Land is specified throughout, with possible purchaser recovery and wife's release; no extension to all movables is made.
i-ketubah.rights: Meiri's living/posthumous rights and widow examples are accurately summarized.
i-ketubah.source-map: Both paragraphs were read against the full introduction and separately attached ending; the shortened snapshot's omission is not treated as disproof.

i-shlichut.kiddushin: Agency validity differs from preference for personal kiddushin; father's authority is distinguished from the prohibition/advice on child marriage.
i-shlichut.get: Authenticated signatures versus messenger's bifnai statement, two delivery witnesses and prior reading are retained.

i-gerushin.meaning: Divorce/death and additional Rabbi Yehudah wording follow sources; local9:3 versus canonical9:2 numbering remains explicit.
i-gerushin.writing: Other languages/scripts are permitted subject to textual clarity; no unconditional any-writing permission is inferred.
i-gerushin.delivery: Woman's presence beside home/courtyard is retained; garment/basket details remain bounded by Rambam's account.
i-gerushin.written-gist: Content and script clarity are both preserved; repeated paragraph does not imply a bare formula is a complete valid get.

i-lishmah.meaning: Learning text, other couple and other wife cases all require specified husband and wife at writing.
i-lishmah.distinction: Undecided wife at writing invalidates get; subsequent priestly disqualification is preserved without calling it valid divorce.

i-edei-get.meaning: Rabbi Elazar follows quoted Mishnah spelling; Rambam spelling variant stays noted. No-signature delivery validity is actually stated.
i-edei-get.distinction: Both paragraphs distinguish absent delivery witnesses, missing signatures, and invalid signed witness producing mezuyaf-mitocho even with proper delivery.

i-yibum.falling: Both paragraphs preserve paternal brother/seed requirement, Torah-ervah exemption and limitations of the yibum/halitzah maxim.
i-yibum.one: One house/one wife/one brother operation follows Rambam's first principle.
i-yibum.ervah: Ervah exemption and co-wife conditions differ from partial maamar obstruction requiring halitzah.
i-yibum.house-rule: Multiple wives and brothers do not each require separate operations; wording remains within the one-house example.

i-chalitzah.meaning: Release from yibum bond and co-wife consequence follow attached Mishnah and Rambam; comparison with get is limited to release.
i-chalitzah.seder: Readings, visible spitting, shoe removal and three-plus-two publicity are retained; no sufficiency claim about abbreviated procedure.
i-chalitzah.advice: Age-matched advice is expressly attributed to Rambam and not presented as current practical practice.
i-chalitzah.publicity: Three judges and two publicity participants remain distinct; lay competence at need is not generalized.

i-maamar.meaning: Maamar is incomplete kiddushin in the cited yibum framework, not completed yibum.
i-maamar.consequence: Actors and order were checked: Shimon dies, Levi is born, Reuven makes maamar, Reuven dies. Leah needs halitzah while Rachel remains ervah.
i-maamar.two-sides: Both stringent effects follow the explicit conclusion despite parenthesized difficult source word; no emendation is claimed.

z-peah.meaning: Peah minimum, enlarged gift and leket at harvest are distinguished from later tithing; examples remain within cited cases.
z-peah.distinction: Owner/worker memory and two-seah single sheaf exclusions remain stated.
z-peah.measure: Increase above minimum follows field size, poor population and yield; no unmentioned factor is supplied.

z-leket-shikcha.leket: Inside versus behind hand/sickle follows Rambam's explicit explanation; not every fallen stalk becomes poor property.
z-leket-shikcha.edge: Edge case's actual outcomes and Rambam's ruling for Rabbi Akiva are retained.
z-leket-shikcha.omer: Single two-seah sheaf differs from two sheaves totaling two seah; Rabbi Gamliel/sages and Rambam's ruling remain distinct.

z-hafrashah.produce: Edibility, guarded ownership and earth growth with ownerless/fungi exclusions follow all four segments.
z-hafrashah.gmar: Ripeness versus finishing and market/home distinctions remain separate; picking alone is not treated as universal fixation.
z-hafrashah.order: Bikkurim/terumah/first/second order and effective-but-prohibited reversal follow Mishnah; terumat-maaser has separate verse.
z-hafrashah.gmar-home: Ripeness, finishing and fixation are not collapsed; house/market difference remains the actual cited explanation.

z-terumah.meaning: Great terumah and terumat-maaser origins/order are distinguished; unstated Torah quantity is accurately reported.
z-terumah.amount: One-fortieth/fiftieth/sixtieth are the Mishnah's main scale; Beit Shammai's beautiful-eye disagreement is not conflated.
z-terumah.who: Owner/agent authority and invalid minor/incapable/nonowner contributions follow Mishnah/Rambam.
z-terumah.cohen: Same-location requirement and additional terumah's tithe liability precede priestly consumption; no blanket exemption of additions.

z-maaser-rishon.gift: Levitical gift and order follow explicit verse, Rambam terminology and Terumot3:6.
z-maaser-rishon.tenth: Tenth of first tithe has its own verse and is distinguished from initial great terumah.
z-maaser-rishon.distinction: Levitical gift differs from sacred second-tithe Jerusalem consumption; one does not discharge the other.

z-maaser-sheni.meaning: Sale/pledge/exchange and weighing restrictions follow sacred status in source.
z-maaser-sheni.pidyon: Distance, money transported to Jerusalem and food use follow verses; purchased food's rules have attached commentary.
z-maaser-sheni.use: Normal consumption, flavor-damaging perfuming prohibition and permitted anointing are all in source.
z-maaser-sheni.fifth: Quarter-of-principal computation is correct; competing offers and evadable added fifth explain preference for larger principal.
z-maaser-sheni.fourth: Repeated computation does not turn the example into permission for every redemption method.

z-maaser-ani.years: Third/sixth years replace second tithe, and poor-gift grouping follows attached source.
z-maaser-ani.biur: Fourth/seventh-year Pesach and gift-to-recipient versus destruction of edible second-tithe/revai remainder remain distinct.

z-demai.meaning: Uncertainty from am-haaretz differs from definite tevel; great terumah assumed given and two remaining obligations are stated.
z-demai.distinction: Prohibition correction differs from monetary claim; Levi/poor burden of proof and ownerless-fruit leniency follow source.

z-challah.grains: Five species and bread analogy follow Mishnah/Rambam; no modern botanical equivalence is newly asserted.
z-challah.dough: Flour separation is invalid; both resulting kneaded amounts can require challah. Forbidden-to-stranger refers to actual separated challah.
z-challah.amount: Threshold versus gift fraction remain distinct; impure-dough cases are explicitly deferred rather than universalized.
z-challah.baker: Both recorded reasons remain attributed. Large wedding dough retains household rate, so size alone is not made decisive.

z-five-grains.species: Both paragraphs distinguish species identity, combination conditions and rooting-before-Omer rule.
z-five-grains.combination: Combination completes required quantity; prose explicitly avoids making every dough attachment equivalent.
z-five-grains.new: Chametz/matzah explanation follows local segment6 with separately identified canonical Challah1:2 crosswalk.

z-orlah.years: Three forbidden years and fourth-year sacred revai are distinguished by verses and Rambam's terminology.
z-orlah.intent: Food versus fence/wood intent and rejected Rabbi Yosei split-tree rule follow source.
z-orlah.chutz: No seeing Orlah harvesting differs from no personally harvesting kilayim; Mishnah and separate MT10:11 witnesses are kept distinct.

z-bikkurim.meaning: Unripe designation versus ripe bringing and rejected Rabbi Shimon re-designation are preserved.
z-bikkurim.distinction: Bringing and recitation categories differ; waving/placement has its separate attached Mishnah.

z-kilayim.kinds: Different prohibition categories are not equated with prohibited benefit from every result.
z-kilayim.crops: Seed mixture's permitted food differs from vineyard mixture's burned/prohibited-benefit result.
z-kilayim.grafting: Diaspora Torah versus rabbinic rules follow Orlah3:9; no content is invented for truncated Kilayim8:1 segment2.

z-sheviit.work: Concise biblical inventory reports the named prohibitions; it does not give practical harvest procedure.
z-sheviit.fruit: Money shares the source's sheviit consequences; human/animal food and dye categories are actually identified.
z-sheviit.use: Human-food medicinal-use restriction differs from other plant use, matching both source clauses.
z-sheviit.price: Source's nonpersistent-in-ground condition is retained for biur; sanctity is not collapsed into biur timing.

z-biur.meaning: Field availability, dried-fig example and regional distinction follow the actual commentary.
z-biur.distinction: Rambam destruction and Ramban abandonment views remain separate; Ramban's delayed-private-retention eating prohibition is retained.
z-biur.regions: Timing in relevant region differs from disagreement over the act of biur; source's difficult detailed map is not reconstructed.

z-shemittat-kesafim.debt: Rambam's unusual document/responsibility explanation is openly attributed; shop account/wages become loans only upon fixation.
z-shemittat-kesafim.disputes: Rabbi Yehudah's prior accounts and Rabbi Yosei's seasonal work positions are stated as rejected views.

z-prozbul.meaning: Hillel's reason and declaration follow Mishnah; included debts are not equated with every possible claim.
z-prozbul.distinction: Rambam's rabbinic-era limitation and court pleading for heir are explicit in source.

d-nezikin.avot: Rambam's shor=regel/maveh=shen reading is attributed; keren is not silently omitted from all liabilities.
d-nezikin.difference: Public-domain shen/regel, vessel bor and hidden-fire exclusions follow named distinctions.
d-nezikin.features: Characteristic harm and specific exemptions remain connected without making the four examples exhaustive.

d-chovel.meaning: Five payments and injury intent sufficient for boshet are preserved; no intent-to-shame-only test remains.
d-chovel.distinction: Both paragraphs distinguish individual payments, doctor-disobedience loss and outside-Israel collection jurisdiction without making all five fines.

d-geneivah.meaning: Full saved Meiri segments1/3 distinguish hiding due to fear from ambush to stop escape; source rationale is attributed, not called a Mishnah quote.
d-geneivah.distinction: Movable/body-value double payment and ox/sheep slaughter/sale fines retain exclusions and confession exemption; local/canonical oath numbering is disclosed.

d-gezel.meaning: Read against both attached sources. Pre-existing partial-versus-total rot wording remains a tentative lexical-scope concern, not a demonstrated legal contradiction.
d-gezel.distinction: Changed wood/wool and grown animal ownership examples follow source; underlying restitution is not erased.

d-shomrim.four: Both paragraphs distinguish paid guardians, borrower exemptions and specific-object oath. Torah/rabbinic oath wording conflict remains disclosed.
d-shomrim.ones: Unavoidable event differs from deliberate exposure; owner's presence at borrowing and negligence exception are preserved.
d-shomrim.baalav: Timing at borrowing and breadth including negligence are separately stated, not inferred from presence at loss.

d-shomer-ones.roles: Four custodians but three responsibility patterns follow Mishnah and verse assignments.
d-shomer-ones.wolves: Both paragraphs were read. Single/two wolves and named dissenting dog/wolf rules are reports of Mishnah opinions; no fresh ruling is inserted.
d-shomer-ones.exposure: Self-introduction to dangerous bands differs from animals arriving themselves, as source states.

d-ribit.meaning: Example-specific Torah interest versus rabbinic fruit-debt arrangement is not universalized to every usage of neshech/tarbit.
d-ribit.distinction: Both paragraphs distinguish pre-existing debt with stock from current-money purchase at known market price, including mi-shepara.

d-avedah.siman: Count can identify two needles; this is a possible identifying sign, not an unconditional all-locations return rule.
d-avedah.recognition: Honest scholar recognition and location/population limits remain alongside the identifying-sign paragraph.

d-karka.ways: All three paragraphs distinguish underlying lien from recovery from purchasers, oral versus documented debt, and local document custom.
d-karka.chazakah: Owner authorization, absent-owner lek-hazak instruction and sale-document payment conditions remain distinct.

d-mitaltelin.meshichah: Goods/currency classification varies by actual circulating use; prose follows Rambam's stated meshichah principle.
d-mitaltelin.agav: House/pepper example preserves explicit agav instruction and remote goods without drawing physical co-location requirement.

d-onaah.meaning: All three numeric examples match Rambam despite distinct denominators; buyer and seller both can be aggrieved.
d-onaah.distinction: One-sixth restitution differs from greater-than-sixth cancellation; seller's missing merchandise explains time difference.
d-onaah.seller-buyer: Buyer's inspection window differs from seller's later comparison opportunity; no universal fixed duration is invented.

d-shutfin.meaning: Divisible courtyard differs from voluntary division; binding allocation precedes wall compulsion.
d-shutfin.distinction: Seeing through gaps is prohibited harm; local material custom does not eliminate opacity requirement.

d-harchakah.meaning: Different hazard mechanisms and separation measures are summarized without giving one common distance.
d-harchakah.distinction: Preexisting-wall exception and non-bor-designated adjoining field condition are preserved.

d-yerushah.meaning: Read the entire Amram family example: descendants exhaust priority before ascending through paternal ancestors.
d-yerushah.distinction: Husband/wife and son/mother are stated in the correct direction; oral-tradition attribution follows Rambam.
d-yerushah.three-laws: Representation by deceased potential heir's successors differs from a list of living relatives alone.

d-chazakah.meaning: Three-year possession requires purchase claim; it is evidence, not an acquiring act at year three.
d-chazakah.distinction: Protest before two, absent possessor and war/interrupted communications qualification are retained.

d-two-chazakot.action: Acquiring act requires seller authorization; no three-year evidentiary use is confused with that act.
d-two-chazakot.proof: Current final refinement retains both purchase claim and fruit-use evidence, with no automatic year-three acquisition.
d-two-chazakot.owner: Final refinement explicitly identifies owner's silence; knowledge/protest opportunity still qualifies inference.

d-shevuot.meaning: Three Torah oaths, partial acknowledgment, minimum values and same-kind condition remain source-bounded.
d-shevuot.distinction: Both paragraphs distinguish defendant's exonerating oath from claimant's oath to collect; refusal does not universally authorize seizure.
d-shevuot.hesset: Both paragraphs preserve claimant/defendant distinction and hesset's different object-holding mode, despite repetition.

d-edut.meaning: Original three-judge panel is separated from expanded five. PHM four-agree/one-unsure addition conflicts with MT majority and remains disclosed.
d-edut.distinction: Formal admission/instruction differs from casual narrative; source does not require only the literal hevu-alai-edim formula.

d-dayanim.three: Chosen third judge's impartiality and sages' choice method follow source.
d-dayanim.acceptance: Expertise, party acceptance and authority to compel are separate; diaspora/specific border-town distinction follows MT4:14-15.
d-dayanim.permission: Accepted lay adjudication differs from lone public expert and geographical coercive authorization.

a-shechitah.meaning: Full two simanim initially versus majority after fact is preserved for bird/beast; vein rule is not confused with siman proportions.
a-shechitah.distinction: Both paragraphs preserve expertise/testing and gentile slaughter, including explicit nonidolater extension from separate MT witness.
a-shechitah.competence: Legal eligibility differs from practical expertise and five disqualifying acts; not a practical slaughter manual.

a-terefah.meaning: Read the full long anatomical source. Defect examples remain subject to their specific criteria; no fresh anatomical correction is made.
a-terefah.distinction: Two esophageal membranes differ from penetrating heart cavity; fall/claw cases require their own examination.
a-terefah.internal: Organ/location/number-of-membranes distinctions are actually in source; visible illness alone is not made decisive.

a-basar-chalav.meaning: Pure domestic mammal differs from wild animal/bird; Rambam's cooking permission and rabbinic eating prohibition remain separate.
a-basar-chalav.distinction: Dining-table decree and Beit Hillel bird inclusion follow explicit habit-of-transgression explanation.
a-basar-chalav.distance: Same eating-table protection is distinguished from Torah cooking prohibition; uncooked juxtaposition is the Mishnah's actual case.

a-taam.meaning: Milk-drop taste case and unlike-kind treatment follow Mishnah/Rambam.
a-taam.distinction: Initial versus later stirring, covering through end and continuing piece prohibition are retained; tasting/sixty discussion is context-bounded.
a-taam.udder: No-tearing-with-other-meat case retains both inclusion toward sixty and udder's own continuing prohibition.

a-neder.meaning: Object prohibition differs from conditional sacrifice obligation upon performing mitzvah; tefillin are not made forbidden.
a-neder.distinction: Incomplete modar formula needs eating-language continuation to prohibit eating, as Rambam explains.
a-neder.sukkah: Specific sukkah prohibition and separate contingent sacrifice model follow source without inventing a new rationale.

a-yadot-kinuyim.names: Incomplete phrase differs from alternate local terminology; kinuy examples have separate MT1:16 prooftext.
a-yadot-kinuyim.meaning: Both paragraphs preserve no eating prohibition without continuation and distinguish Akiva's tentative prohibition from lashes.
a-yadot-kinuyim.rashaim: Both paragraphs preserve explicit continuation requirement; bare knidrei-reshaim does not itself impose all three obligations.

a-hatarah.meaning: Knowledge that anger/vowing is wrong does not itself release vow; sage release differs from bounded paternal/husband annulment.
a-hatarah.distinction: Betrothed girl's father and husband act jointly; neither alone is made sufficient.

a-shevuah.meaning: Future/past oath fourfold inventory differs from court monetary oath.
a-shevuah.distinction: One implicit eating/drinking oath differs from two expressly divided prohibitions.
a-shevuah.speech: Current paragraph follows explicit wording's role in number of liabilities; no reversed causal phrasing remains.

olah.purpose: Burned flesh, obligatory/voluntary distinction and named daily/festival/pilgrimage/childbirth/nazir offerings follow the cited Introduction body, not translator preface.
olah.animals: Male livestock versus either-sex specified-age birds and fixed daily lambs match Intro14/16/22; no free substitution across obligations.
olah.service: North reception, diagonal two/four applications and stripping/cutting follow Mishnah5:4 and Rambam's explicit explanation.
olah.portions: All flesh burned does not include skin; Intro37 explicitly assigns animal-olah skin to priests.
olah.bird: Read entire procedural sequence: head salted/burned before body preparation; lower animal versus upper bird blood is explicit. Described nonseparation of body is the prescribed procedure, not a claim that accidental separation invalidates.
olah.neder: Both paragraphs retain personal obligation versus designated animal and obligation not discharged by unlike-offering intent; remaining service is still completed as olah.
olah.analysis: Distinct blood/skin/cutting operations follow actual Mishnah sequence; no whole-animal-burning rule is inferred.

chattat.purpose: Main inadvertent-karet rule is bounded and explicitly excludes Pesach/milah; childbirth/zav/metzora/nazir obligations do not invent a niddah offering from difficult Intro36.
chattat.animals: Individual/ruler/anointed-priest distinction is bounded to ordinary fixed chattat; idolatry is separated and public species are not generalized.
chattat.variable: Livestock/bird/flour economic scale follows Intro35 for sanctuary impurity; no claim every chattat has a poverty substitution.
chattat.outer: North, four corners, south remainder, male-priest courtyard/time and midnight fence follow Mishnah and Z5:3.
chattat.inner: Both paragraphs preserve emurim versus burned body and distinguish Yom-Kippur between-poles applications from other internal offerings.
chattat.bird: No head separation, lower-wall sprinkling/remainder and all-priest flesh follow Mishnah6:4; upper bird-olah contrast is accurate.
chattat.shem: Other sacred offering versus hullin intention and unstated intention have their distinct outcomes in Z1:1; no all-unlike-intent invalidation remains.

k-inner-chattat.place: Between-poles versus curtain/gold altar applications and north slaughter are separately stated; upper external blood is not confused with inside.
k-inner-chattat.essential: Both paragraphs follow all-required inner applications and partial-time-thought no-karet treatment in Z4:2; not every defective thought is called piggul.
k-inner-chattat.remainder: West remainder is explicitly nonessential, while inside applications are essential; body burning is separately described.

shelamim.purpose: Private altar/priest/owner portions and voluntary versus pilgrimage duty follow sources; public holiness/eating differs.
shelamim.animals: Livestock either sex versus no birds is explicit; specified nazir ram limits free species choice.
shelamim.service: All-courtyard slaughter and city consumption remain different places; blood two/four applications follow source.
shelamim.portions: Priests' household eating is bounded to eligible recipients; owner flesh and emurim remain distinct.
shelamim.time: Two days/one night is contrasted with todah/nazir's shorter duration, including raised priestly portions.
shelamim.tenufa-depth: Living semichah versus postslaughter waving and owner/priest hand positions follow Menachot. General procedural account is qualified by separate person blocks excluding women's own acts.

todah.nature: Todah is a special shelamim with bread and shorter eating period; vow wording is actually in Intro41.
todah.bread: All four types and forty loaves counted; ten chametz equal thirty matzah by flour amount, not number; one each to priest.
todah.portions: Emurim burned, breast/thigh plus four loaves to priest, remaining flesh/bread to owners; priestly loaves are eaten rather than a kometz.
todah.service: Two/four blood, Jerusalem and midnight rabbinic fence follow Z5:6; dawn is the stated Torah endpoint.
todah.bread-ratio: Repeated comparison correctly separates number of loaves from aggregate flour.

nazir.purpose: Completion's yearling olah/ewe chattat and ram shelamim differ from impurity asham; correct sexes and species retained.
nazir.service: Nazir ram follows light-holy shelamim slaughter/blood/emurim rules.
nazir.portions: Cooked foreleg, breast/thigh and two specified loaves follow Z5:6; remainder belongs to owner.
nazir.time: Jerusalem/day-night-midnight and eligible priestly recipients follow todah analogy, without using ordinary two-day shelamim period.

bekhor.nature: Male first-womb and unblemished offering follow verse/Intro38; obligation is not introduced as a personal vow.
bekhor.service: Single application toward foundation differs from ordinary shelamim despite shared light holiness.
bekhor.eating: Priestly Jerusalem two-day/one-night consumption and duty to offer/eat sacredly follow actual witnesses.

maaser.nature: Counted tenth differs from selecting one of ten; rejected Rabbi Yosei bar-Yehudah position remains identified. Prescribed red-marking procedure is not said to invalidate when omitted.
maaser.service: Light holiness, one foundation-facing application and emurim follow Mishnah5:8/Z5:8.
maaser.eating: Owner's two-day/one-night meat includes breast/thigh; no priestly special share is invented.

pesach.purpose: Fourteenth after afternoon tamid and private-like-public scheduled-offering category follow both attached sources.
pesach.service: Courtyard/single foundation-facing application and enrolled-group consumption follow Mishnah5:8.
pesach.eating: Midnight is expressly attached to the Mishnah and Rambam's local Torah-language presentation; unresolved end-time dispute is acknowledged rather than explained by importing todah's fence.
pesach.shem: At-time versus other-times reversal is exactly the saved Z1:1 explanation, with practical qualifications left to its context.
pesach.scope: Read full saved Meiri introduction segment2; hametz checking/removal, matzah/maror and seder-night subjects are actually listed. New independent Meiri edition remains unavailable.

k-nesachim.meaning: All seven verse segments read; lamb quarter, ram third and cattle half-hin oil/wine accompany one/two/three flour measures.
k-nesachim.distinction: Five excluded offering categories and metzora chattat/asham exception are explicit; non-sin rationale is attributed to source.

av-semichah.act: Two hands, head, same slaughter place and no intervening act follow Mishnah/Rambam.
av-semichah.offerings: Private exclusions and two public exceptions are distinguished; rejected Rabbi Shimon idolatry-goat extension is not adopted.
av-semichah.person: Owner not agent, every partner separately, and named personal exemptions follow both Mishnayot.
av-semichah.effect: Already-effected atonement differs from missing command; source's as-if-not-atoned phrase is not turned into actual invalidity.

av-shechitah.act: Both simanim initially versus majority after fact applies in kodashim; neck/vessel arrangement does not merge reception with slaughter.
av-shechitah.person: Lay/woman/slave initial validity differs from impure-person decree. Long knife or unlawful entry explains physical possibility and is not a permission to ignore decree.
av-shechitah.place: Animal most-holy north differs from light-holy all courtyard; semichah proximity applies where required, as separate exceptions state.
av-shechitah.thought: Eligibility for the performed service governs disqualifying thought; lack of priesthood alone does not exclude slaughter thoughts.

av-kabbalah.act: Direct neck life-blood, not skin/residual blood or pre-vessel floor collection, is preserved.
av-kabbalah.person: Both paragraphs retain fit priest, standing, hand/foot noninterposition and right-hand ruling; source's conflicting purification-parenthesis is not resolved here.
av-kabbalah.place: North reception and metzora's partly-hand reception exception are both stated.
av-kabbalah.repair: Still-remaining life-blood condition and fit priest's new valid reception remain explicit; invalid worker's thought is not equated with fit worker's.

av-zerikah.act: Four-service label does not impose one physical blood method; corners/walls/inside and bird/beast differ.
av-zerikah.outer: All three labeled items inspected: chattat four, olah/asham/shelamim two/four, bekhor/maaser/pesach one toward foundation.
av-zerikah.height: Animal chattat/olah versus bird reversal and upper versus inside distinction follow actual sources.
av-zerikah.inner: Yom-Kippur between-poles exception is retained rather than generalized to all inner offerings.
av-zerikah.meakev: Beit Hillel's one essential outer application differs from full initial obligation and all-essential inner gifts.
av-zerikah.shirayim: West inner/south outer remainders and nonessential inner pouring follow source's principal-versus-remainder explanation.

k-matanot.outer: Both paragraphs distinguish initial obligations from essential atonement and first versus later thought consequences.
k-matanot.shammai: Beit Shammai two essential chattat gifts versus Beit Hillel one is preserved; no four independently essential outer gifts asserted.
k-matanot.inner: Both paragraphs keep all-required inner gifts and invalid-but-no-karet mixed-thought case without relabeling it complete piggul.

av-haktarah.act: Animal olah burned flesh after stripping/cutting differs from edible-offering emurim and remainder.
av-haktarah.order: Fire/wood/parts layering and washing entrails/legs before burning follow all three verses.
av-haktarah.burning: Both paragraphs distinguish off-altar body burning and minchah kometz/levonah; common-vessel condition and Rabbi Yosei/sages dispute remain.
av-haktarah.altar: Fit-for-altar qualification prevents treating ascent as cure-all; unvessel-sanctified kometz and Rabbi Yehoshua ruling follow source.

av-melikah.act: Nape and head separation differ for bird chattat/olah; difficult grip description is attributed, not reconstructed.
av-melikah.blood: Lower bird chattat is linked to foundation remainder, upper olah to omitted foundation, and animal reversal remains distinct.
av-melikah.portions: Full paragraph read. Grouped head/body preparation compresses Mishnah6:5's separate sequence and warrants low-severity clarification; detailed olah/bird already states correct order.

av-tenufah.act: Moving/lifting directions and emurim/breast/thigh hand arrangement match source; semichah remains a separate act.
av-tenufah.objects: Living and nonliving objects are both actually listed; bikkurim attribution/Rambam adoption is preserved.
av-tenufah.when: All three labeled items read: private, public and metzora each have the correct two-of-three semichah/living/postslaughter operations.
av-tenufah.person: Woman's offering needs waving but she does not wave; one partner can wave for all, and two loaves/lambs lie beside each other.

avodot.sequence: All four labeled service items inspected; direct neck reception and variable physical application remain distinct.
avodot.worker: Initial lay/woman/slave slaughter validity differs from priestly reception onward; right-hand dispute is retained.
avodot.place: Moriah sanctuary exclusivity differs from within-courtyard slaughter zones and Jerusalem eating; no citywide slaughter permission.

imurim.parts: Named fats/kidneys/liver appendage and sheep tail follow Intro20/21; remaining meat has offering-dependent treatment.
imurim.boundaries: Mishkan curtains correspond to courtyard, city to Jerusalem; recipient/place/time are not collapsed.

pesulim.shem: Known private-owner scope, chattat/pesach exceptions, hullin and unstated intent follow Z1:1.
pesulim.place: Usual eating/burning object condition and invalid/no-piggul-karet outcome follow Z2:2/3.
pesulim.time: Proper completion of permissive service and fit thinker restrict piggul; any other invalidity is not casually called piggul.
pesulim.notar: Later leftover meat after valid service differs from service-time bad intention and does not undo original owner's discharge.
pesulim.example: Next-day ordinary shelamim eating differs from expired todah window; remaining piggul conditions are expressly retained.
pesulim.essential-parts: Outer first essential versus subsequent gifts differs from all-required inner gifts, following both commentaries.

k-meilah.meaning: Inadvertence/value conditions are retained; no-meilah does not automatically grant ordinary use, and not-enjoy/no-meilah remains prohibited.
k-meilah.distinction: South-slaughter invalidity does not extinguish meilah; prior permitted-to-priest time is the separate dividing criterion.
k-meilah.invalid-service: Both paragraphs retain possible meilah despite invalid service and distinguish terminology from prohibition. Return by fit priests may establish permission only in source's available-blood setting.

k-temurah.meaning: Prohibited act differs from effective transfer; both animals remain holy when effective. Unequal negative/positive-command scope explains lashes in this saved Commentary.
k-temurah.distinction: Public/partnership non-effect and priestly gift ownership do not collapse into permission to exchange.
k-temurah.ownership: Separate questions of violation and new-animal holiness follow explicit not-every-exchanger-effects-exchange rule.

public.public: Daily/additional offerings, two Shavuot peace lambs and absence of public asham follow Intro18/22/25.
public.time: Scheduled time rather than public label governs; unappointed public sins and compensable pilgrimage offerings retain their exceptions.
